about.title: About Goa
about.lede: Goa grew out of spreadsheets — the ones a group of friends kept to run a film club and a reading club. It automates that work: people log their progress, the system does the maths, and the result becomes a memory.
body: The idea is simple. A group picks a challenge — watch a list of films, read for 90 days, keep a habit — and each person logs their progress. Goa handles the rest: it tracks who's on schedule, computes averages and rankings, and at the end builds a showcase that tells the story of that round.
Nothing is public by default. Every group is private, access always comes from belonging to it, and submitted entries are preserved — only the curation and presentation stay editable.
Goa is a personal project in progress, built by Eduardo Dourado. The original spreadsheets became the domain spec; the app is gradually catching up to everything they did, with far less manual work.
about.librariesTitle: How Goa organises what you track
libraries: Each personal space and each group keeps its own libraries — the lists of things you track. Screens is the broader evolution of Movies: films, series, seasons, episodes, documentaries, or whatever unit you choose. Pages is the broader evolution of Books, and also holds articles and other reading. Tables is a configurable starting point for places like restaurants, bars and cafés. You can create more specific libraries of your own, such as Matches or TV Shows — and rename, hide or reorder every property of any of them. A single challenge can draw from several libraries at once — Movies and TV Shows in one list.

You decide what one item represents. A trilogy can be one item or three; a season can be one item or every episode. Goa doesn't guess: fill in duration, pages or year only when you know them. An average episode duration and a total runtime are different numbers, and mixing them would make time totals wrong.

Done means the item's required answers are in — nothing more. For a football match it can simply mean “I tracked this one”; you don't have to have watched it. An answer everyone shares, like a final score, is recorded once for the group, while ratings and comments stay individual. If two people edit a shared answer at once, the second is told and shown the latest value instead of overwriting it.

Recommendations say where an item came from: a member, someone outside the group you've saved by name, or a short note. Groups can switch them off entirely. Items can also carry an optional schedule — whole days or an exact time — that feeds an agenda. A due date is only a reminder: it never stops anyone from answering.

affinity.title: Affinities
affinity.explanation: Similarity of ratings in this challenge — 100 × (1 − mean absolute difference ÷ scale). Not a personal compatibility score.
affinity.compositeNote: Composite affinity needs enough shared items per genre, year and length — shown once the data is there.

explain.sum: Adds up every value recorded for this field.
explain.average: The simple average: the sum of all the values divided by how many there are.
explain.count: How many valid records there are.
explain.median: The middle value once everything is sorted (with an even count, the average of the two middle ones).
explain.completion_rate: Completed records divided by everything expected, times 100.
explain.bayesian_average: A fair average for ranking. An item with only a few ratings is pulled toward the overall average of the whole list, so a single enthusiastic vote can't put it on top. The more ratings it has, the closer it gets to its own simple average (the plain figure is shown underneath). Formula: (n × item average + {weight} × overall average) ÷ (n + {weight}), where n is the item's number of ratings.
explain.spread: How much the ratings disagree (population standard deviation): the higher it is, the more the group was divided.
explain.consensus: How much the group agrees, from 0 to 100 — 100 means everyone gave the same rating.
explain.surprise: Rating minus expectation, using pairs where the same person gave both for the same item. Positive means it beat expectations.
explain.indicator_bias: The average of the items each person recommended minus the overall average — how well their recommendations landed.

wrapped.explainMinimum: Only shown once there are at least {minimum, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}.

libraries.newBody: A library is a list of things you track together — places, matches, games, anything. Start from a preset or from a blank page.
libraries.blankHint: Just a name. Add the properties you want.
libraries.tablesPresetHint: For restaurants, bars and cafés — cuisine, neighbourhood and address to start.
libraries.renameHint: Only the name changes — its items and properties stay as they are.
libraries.propertiesBody: Rename, hide or reorder what each item in this library can hold. Hiding a property keeps what's already saved — it just stops appearing.
libraries.propertiesReadOnly: What each item in this library can hold.
libraries.propertyHiddenSaved: Property hidden. Saved values are kept.
libraries.addPropertyHint: For example Cuisine, Score or Stage.
libraries.scheduleHint: When the item itself happens — a match's kick-off. Switch it on and every challenge using these items reads the same date. It's separate from when answers may be given.

catalogAdd.orCreateNew: Otherwise, fill in the rest and add it as a new item.
